title: Staged Traffic Playbook Engine: policy-driven rollouts, A/B/shadow routing, and automated rollback
creator: Marina Lopez
description: Implement a reusable "playbook" engine for staged traffic deployments that codifies traffic splits, step schedules, hold/extend semantics, guardrails, and automated rollback actions. The playbook combines A/B experiments, shadow traffic routing, and canary ramps into a policy-first engine that operators and Product/Design can author via Console or YAML. Goals: (1) reduce toil for safe rollouts across hosted/dedicated/private deployments, (2) provide deterministic, SLO-driven rollback behavior, and (3) surface simulation/dry-run to validate policies before traffic changes.
acceptance_criteria: Operators can create a staged traffic playbook in Console or via YAML that declares: ordered steps, target traffic split per step, step duration, cooldown, conditional holds, and rollback rules.
Playbook engine will execute ramps against the runtime and update routing state with atomic step boundaries; changes are visible in Console rollout timeline and via rw rollout CLI.

Automatic rollback triggers when composite risk score exceeds threshold for a configured evaluation window. Risk score combines p95 latency delta, error rate delta, and quality-regression signal from evaluation prompts.
Support for shadow traffic mode where a fraction of live traffic is forked to candidate variant without impacting user responses; shadowing can be enabled per-step.
A/B experiment templates supported: statistical test configuration (metric, test type), minimum sample size, and optional lookback windows.
Simulation mode: dry-run validates policy against historical traffic profile and emits a timeline with predicted metric deltas; no routing changes performed.
Telemetry: per-playbook metrics (step, percent, risk_score, hold_count), traces sampled and tagged for playbook_id; Console shows token-level cost delta estimate per step.
E2E tests and integration tests covering rollback, hold-on-failure, shadow traffic correctness, and CLI-config parsing are added and green in CI.
tasks: Design: finalise playbook YAML schema and Console schema editor (Design + PM)
Runtime: implement staged-step applier with atomic commit and rollback hook
Policy Engine: risk scoring, SLO adapters, and rule evaluator
Routing: extend router to support percent splits + shadow fork per route
Console: rollout UI for authoring, timeline, and simulation dry-run
CLI: add rw rollout apply/dry-run/status commands
QA: add synthetic load tests and chaos scenarios to verify rollback behavior
Docs: quickstart, playbook examples (ab test, shadowing, blue-green), and operator runbook
implementation_notes: Engine is model-agnostic and should operate using routing primitives exposed by the serving runtime. Risk scoring will initially be computed from metrics emitted by runtime (latency p50/p95, error-rate) + a lightweight quality hook that can POST evaluations to Optimize. Default thresholds: risk_score > 0.6 for 3 consecutive evaluation windows triggers rollback; hold when p95 delta > 40% for window. Allow project-level overrides and tenant-safe defaults. Persist playbook state in rollout service's compact state machine; ensure idempotent step application and durable rollback markers for audit. Use feature flag to gate Console UI until ergonomics validated.
discussion: 2026-03-02 Marina Lopez: Draft schema posted to Confluence. Proposal uses 'steps' array with optional 'shadow' boolean and 'ab_test' object. Asking for feedback on default cooldown semantics.

2026-03-04 Jacob Kim: Proposed runtime API for atomic step commit described in PR 1423. Concern: committing step across multi-region pools must be transactional; suggested approach is two-phase apply with fast-failover route fallback.
2026-03-05 Priya Narang (PM): Product prefers explicit 'hold' state that requires manual release by default for high-risk endpoints; recommend configurable default per project.
2026-03-07 Design review: Added UI mockups for timeline and simulation overlay. UX asks for clear color coding for shadow vs live split and a rollback CTA in timeline.

2026-03-09 Reliability review (SRE): Agreed on sampling topology for traces and recommended telemetry tag 'playbook_id' + 'step_index'. SRE requested backpressure limits to avoid overloaded inference pools during rapid ramps.
2026-03-10 Jacob Kim: Implementation spike complete; created branch 'playbook-engine' and initial unit tests for YAML parser. Next PR will include router split support and simulation harness.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Rapid ramps could overload GPU pools in Dedicated customers. Mitigation: enforce ramp-rate limits and autoscaling cooldown integration; default conservative percent increases.

Risk: False positives from noisy metrics cause unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: composite risk score with smoothing window and requirement for sustained breach across windows; allow manual overrides and canary hold.
Risk: Shadowing increases downstream processing cost. Mitigation: support sampled shadowing and replay-to-batched-eval pipelines to keep cost bounded.
Risk: Cross-region divergence during step commit. Mitigation: two-phase commit + fallback routing policy that routes to last-known-good variant when commit fails on subset of regions.
